paragraphs.text: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that records the harness's own runtime warnings and errors to stderr, so a
boot that fails after startup can say why.
# dsh-plugin-log-bridge
**A DeepSeek Harness plugin that writes the harness's own runtime warnings and errors to stderr, so
a boot that fails after startup can say why.**
The harness keeps its log records in an in-memory ring and exports them nowhere. An error that happe

ns after
startup — a session that cannot activate, a preset that fails to mount — leaves no trace on

ce the process is
gone, so whatever supervises the process can only report *that* the boot failed, n

ot *why*. Warnings are worse:
the default exporter level filters them out of the ring entirely.
This plugin attaches an exporter that writes every `error` and `warn` to **stderr**, which any super

visor
already captures, and records session-activation failures the same way.
> **Project status:** 1.0.0. Verified against the DeepSeek Harness **0.1.x** composition it was writ

ten for,
> where it was exercised in the desktop app that bundles it. **Not yet verified inside the

official DeepSeek
> Harness desktop app (0.2.0-rc.2)** — that verification is pending. The plugin ha

s no UI and requires no other
> package, so the surface it touches is small.
## Why this exists
A harness that fails to start is the worst possible time to have no diagnostics. When it fails *afte

r* the
ready line — when a session cannot activate, or a plugin row throws — the process exits and t

akes its log ring
with it. The only record is whatever the parent process chose to capture.
Node's own stderr survives the process, which makes it the one durable channel available without add

ing a logger
dependency. This plugin uses nothing else: it imports nothing at module scope, so there

is nothing for the
loader to resolve and nothing that can fail to install.
## What it does
- **Bridges `error` and `warn` records** to stderr, one prefixed line per record, with stack traces

indented
under their first line.
- **Replays the buffered errors** that were logged before the plugi

n loaded. Warnings from that window are
already gone — the default level filtered them out of the ri

ng before this plugin existed — and the README
says so rather than pretending otherwise.
- **Records

session-activation failures** from `api-session/error`, which never reach the logger at all.
- **Ra
te-limits itself**: 100 messages per 60-second window, then a single line saying how many were dropp

ed.
An error in a loop cannot flood the log.
- **Writes a ready line once per launch**, so a log wit

hout it can be read as predating the bridge.
- **Cannot break the boot.** Every attachment step is w

rapped. A bridge that can take down the startup it
exists to explain would be worse than no bridge.
## How it works
`apply(ctx)` does three things, each in its own `try`:

1. If `ctx.logger.buffer` is an array, it replays the buffered `error` records.
2. It attaches an ex

porter with `levels: { default: 2 }` (Cordis levels: error 0, info 1, warn 2) to
`ctx.logger`.
3. It
subscribes to `api-session/error` for session-activation failures.
Every write goes through one rate-limited writer. Each line carries the prefix `[harness-log]`, and

that prefix
matters: a loader that inspects stderr to decide which plugin broke a boot can skip pref

ixed lines, so bridged
runtime chatter can never change which plugin a recovery pass blames.

The module exports its formatting and rate-limiting helpers (`formatMessage`, `bridgeLines`,
`create
LimitedWriter`) as pure functions with an injectable clock, so they can be exercised without a harne
itedWriter`) as pure functions with an injectable clock, so they can be exercised without a harness.
## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or later (the harness ships its own; you do not need a separate install).
- A DeepSeek

Harness profile that can load a plugin bundle — 0.1.x or 0.2.x.
- A parent process that captures the
child's stderr. Running `dsh` in a terminal satisfies this.

### Install into the desktop app
Point the app at this folder with `--add-plugin <path>`, or use the official app's plugin manager to

install
the npm package. Installing adds the bundle row; the exported lines then appear on stderr b

eside the harness's
own output.
### Build from source
There is nothing to build. The package is two source files and a patch:

### Smoke test
The pure helpers are testable with no harness at all:

Expect a formatted message and two prefixed lines, the second indented.
## Configuration
There is none. The bridge has no `Config` schema and takes no options, by design — a diagnostic that

needs
configuring is not the one you want when something is broken at boot.
The constants that could reasonably be tuned live at the top of `index.js` and are deliberately not
tants that could reasonably be tuned live at the top of `index.js` and are deliberately not exposed:
| Constant | Value | Meaning |

| `EXPORT_LEVEL` | `2` | Admit up to `warn` (error 0, info 1, warn 2) |
| `WINDOW_MS` | `60_000` | R

ate-limit window |
| `WINDOW_LIMIT` | `100` | Lines per window before dropping |
## Slots used
None. This is a host-only plugin; it contributes no UI and registers into no slot.
## Where things live
| Piece | Path |

| Host half | `index.js` |
| Bundle patch | `cordis.patch.yml` — inserts the row `desktop-log-bridge

` |
| Bridged lines | on the harness's **stderr**, each prefixed `[harness-log]` |
| Ready line | on
**stdout**, once per launch |
## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| No `[harness-log]` lines at all | Nothing has logged an error or warning yet | Force one with a de

liberately broken plugin, or check that the row is in the profile |
[该节后续省略]
## Security
This plugin writes harness log output to **stderr**. That output can contain prompt text, file paths

, tool
arguments and error messages — anything the harness or a plugin chose to log as an error or a

warning. It does
not redact. Treat captured stderr with the same care as the session logs themselve

s, and do not paste it into
a public issue without reading it first.
It makes no network calls, reads no credentials and writes no files.
Report a vulnerability through the process in SECURITY.md.
